title: WHO: heart attacks and many strokes are blockages, often from fatty deposits
summary: WHO says heart attacks and strokes are usually acute events caused mainly by a blockage, most often from fatty deposits, and that strokes can also be bleeds.
body: WHO's cardiovascular-disease fact sheet says heart attacks and strokes are usually acute events and are mainly caused by a blockage that prevents blood from flowing to the heart or brain. It says the most common reason is a build-up of fatty deposits on the inner walls of the blood vessels that supply the heart or brain. It says strokes can also be caused by bleeding from a blood vessel in the brain or by blood clots. That is the mechanism the sheet states. It is not a claim about any one patient's arteries.
